flag_description: Afghanistan's flag consists of three vertical bands of black, red, and green, with the national emblem centered on the flag, though the design and emblem used have varied under different governments.
short_history: Afghanistan's history places it at the crossroads of Central and South Asia, a position that made it a corridor for empires from Alexander the Great to the Mongols and a hub along the Silk Road. The modern Afghan state emerged in 1747 under Ahmad Shah Durrani. Afghanistan resisted British attempts at control during the nineteenth-century Anglo-Afghan Wars and gained full independence in foreign affairs in 1919. The late twentieth century brought a Soviet invasion in 1979, a decade-long war, civil conflict, Taliban rule, a US-led intervention after 2001, and the Taliban's return to power in 2021 following the withdrawal of foreign forces.
interesting_fact: Afghanistan is one of the world's most mountainous countries.
neighbors: Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, China

flag_description: A red flag with a black double-headed eagle in the center.
short_history: Albania's history traces back to the ancient Illyrians before centuries of Roman, Byzantine, and later Ottoman rule beginning in the fifteenth century, during which national hero Skanderbeg famously resisted Ottoman expansion. Albania declared independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1912. The twentieth century brought a brief monarchy, Italian and German occupation during World War II, and then more than four decades of isolated, hardline communist rule under Enver Hoxha until 1985. Albania transitioned to a multiparty democracy in the early 1990s and has since pursued closer integration with Europe, including formal candidacy for European Union membership.
interesting_fact: Albania has one of the largest numbers of bunkers per capita due to its communist-era defense policy.

flag_description: A vertical green and white bicolor with a red crescent and star.
short_history: Algeria's history includes ancient Berber civilizations and periods of Phoenician, Roman, and Arab influence, with Arabization and Islamization following the seventh-century conquests. The Ottoman Empire held nominal control over the coast for centuries before France invaded in 1830 and formally annexed the territory, ruling it as an integral part of France for over a century. Algeria's war of independence, waged from 1954 to 1962, was one of the twentieth century's most brutal anticolonial conflicts, costing hundreds of thousands of lives before independence was achieved in 1962. The following decades brought a civil war in the 1990s and, more recently, mass protests leading to political reform.
interesting_fact: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.
neighbors: Tunisia, Libya, Niger, Mali, Mauritania, Western Sahara, Morocco

flag_description: A vertical blue, yellow and red tricolor with the national coat of arms.
short_history: Andorra's origins as a distinct political entity trace to a legend crediting Charlemagne with granting the valley a charter, though its documented history as a co-principality begins with a 1278 agreement between the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix, establishing joint sovereignty that, remarkably, continues today through the President of France and the Spanish bishop as co-princes. This unusual governance structure allowed Andorra to remain largely isolated and neutral through centuries of European conflict. A modern constitution adopted in 1993 introduced full democratic government while retaining the ceremonial co-princes, and the country has since developed a prosperous economy based on tourism, skiing, and banking.
interesting_fact: Andorra is one of Europe's smallest countries.

flag_description: A horizontal red and black flag with a yellow emblem consisting of a machete, star and half gear.
short_history: Angola's history includes the powerful Kingdom of Kongo and Ndongo before Portuguese colonization, beginning in the fifteenth century, made the territory a major center of the transatlantic slave trade for over three centuries. Portugal maintained colonial control until Angola achieved independence in 1975 following an armed liberation struggle. Independence was immediately followed by a devastating civil war between rival liberation movements that lasted, with interruptions, until 2002 and drew in Cold War-era foreign intervention from Cuba, the Soviet Union, South Africa, and the United States. Since the war's end, Angola has rebuilt its economy around substantial offshore oil reserves.
interesting_fact: Angola has large offshore petroleum reserves.
neighbors: Namibia, Zambia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo

flag_description: A red flag surrounding a blue, white and black design with a rising golden sun.
short_history: Antigua and Barbuda's history includes early settlement by Indigenous Siboney and later Arawak and Carib peoples before Christopher Columbus encountered the islands in 1493. English colonization began in the seventeenth century, and the islands became a center of sugar production dependent on enslaved African labor, with Antigua's Nelson's Dockyard serving as an important British naval base. Slavery was abolished in the British Empire in 1834. Antigua and Barbuda gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1981, retaining the British monarch as head of state within the Commonwealth. Tourism has since become the twin-island nation's dominant economic sector.
interesting_fact: The country consists primarily of the islands of Antigua and Barbuda.

flag_description: Three horizontal bands of light blue, white and light blue with the Sun of May in the center.
short_history: Argentina's history includes Indigenous peoples across its diverse regions before Spanish colonization established Buenos Aires in the sixteenth century as part of the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata. Argentina declared independence from Spain in 1816, and the nineteenth century brought territorial consolidation, waves of European immigration, and rapid economic growth that made Argentina one of the world's wealthiest nations by the early twentieth century. Political instability followed, including repeated military coups and a brutal military dictatorship from 1976 to 1983 marked by the forced disappearance of thousands of dissidents. Argentina returned to democracy in 1983 and remains one of South America's largest economies.
interesting_fact: Argentina is home to Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia.

flag_description: Three horizontal bands of red, blue and orange.
short_history: Armenia's history stretches back over three thousand years, and it became the first nation to adopt Christianity as a state religion in 301 CE. Over subsequent centuries, Armenian territory was repeatedly contested by Persian, Byzantine, and Ottoman empires. The early twentieth century brought the Armenian Genocide of 1915 to 1923, during which the Ottoman government killed an estimated 1.5 million Armenians, an event central to national memory though still disputed by Türkiye. Armenia became part of the Soviet Union before restoring independence in 1991. Since independence, Armenia has faced ongoing tension with Azerbaijan over the Nagorno-Karabakh region.
interesting_fact: Armenia was the first state to adopt Christianity as a state religion.

flag_description: A blue ensign featuring the Union Jack, Commonwealth Star and Southern Cross.
short_history: Australia's history includes Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, whose presence spans more than 60,000 years, making it home to one of the world's oldest continuous cultures. British colonization began in 1788 with the establishment of a penal colony at Sydney, followed by further settlement that dispossessed Indigenous peoples of their land. The six British colonies federated in 1901 to form the Commonwealth of Australia, which gradually gained full legislative independence, formalized by the Statute of Westminster and later the Australia Act of 1986. Modern Australia has developed a multicultural society through sustained immigration and is undertaking ongoing efforts toward reconciliation with Indigenous communities.
interesting_fact: Australia is both a country and a continent.

short_history: Austria's history centers on the Habsburg dynasty, which ruled from Vienna for nearly six centuries and built one of Europe's most powerful empires, the Austro-Hungarian Empire, until its collapse at the end of World War I in 1918. The interwar First Republic was followed by annexation into Nazi Germany in 1938 and subsequent occupation by Allied powers after World War II. Austria regained full sovereignty in 1955 through the Austrian State Treaty, on the condition of permanent neutrality. It joined the European Union in 1995 and has since developed into a prosperous, stable Central European democracy known for its cultural heritage.
interesting_fact: The Austrian flag is among the world's oldest national flag designs.
neighbors: Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland, Liechtenstein

flag_description: A horizontal blue, red and green tricolor with a white crescent and eight-pointed star on the red band.
short_history: Azerbaijan's history in the South Caucasus includes periods of Persian, Arab, and Ottoman influence, and it briefly became the first secular democratic republic in the Muslim world in 1918 before Soviet annexation in 1920. As part of the Soviet Union, Azerbaijan became a major center of oil production. It restored independence in 1991, but the early independence period was dominated by a war with Armenia over the Nagorno-Karabakh region. Azerbaijan regained control over most of the territory following a 2020 conflict and a further 2023 military operation. The country's economy remains heavily reliant on oil and natural gas exports.
interesting_fact: Azerbaijan is known as the Land of Fire because of its natural gas flames and historic fire traditions.

flag_description: A black triangle at the hoist with horizontal aquamarine and gold bands.
short_history: The Bahamas' history begins with the Indigenous Lucayan people, who were the first to encounter Christopher Columbus's expedition in 1492, marking the first recorded landfall of European contact in the Americas. English settlement began in the seventeenth century, and the islands later became notorious as a haven for pirates before coming under formal British colonial administration. The Bahamas became independent from the United Kingdom in 1973, retaining the British monarch as head of state within the Commonwealth. Since independence, tourism and offshore financial services have become the backbone of the Bahamian economy, drawing on the islands' proximity to North America.
interesting_fact: The Bahamas consists of hundreds of islands and cays.

flag_description: A white field at the hoist separated from a red field by a serrated line.
short_history: Bahrain's history as a trading hub stretches back to the ancient Dilmun civilization, which flourished in the region thousands of years ago due to its strategic position in the Persian Gulf. The islands were later ruled by various regional powers before the Al Khalifa family established control in 1783, a dynasty that continues to rule today. Bahrain became a British protectorate in the nineteenth century and gained full independence in 1971. The discovery of oil in 1932, the first in the Gulf, transformed Bahrain's economy, which has since diversified into banking and finance while the country has periodically faced political tensions between its Sunni monarchy and Shia-majority population.
interesting_fact: Bahrain was one of the earliest Gulf locations where oil was discovered.

flag_description: A dark green field with a red disk slightly offset toward the hoist.
short_history: Bangladesh's history is tied to the broader Bengal region, which was a center of trade and culture for centuries before British colonial rule incorporated it into British India. The 1947 partition of British India placed the region, then known as East Bengal and later East Pakistan, under Pakistani administration despite being geographically separated from West Pakistan by India. Political, linguistic, and economic grievances culminated in the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971, a brutal nine-month conflict that resulted in independence with support from India. Since independence, Bangladesh has developed one of the world's fastest-growing economies, notably through its garment manufacturing industry.
interesting_fact: Bangladesh is home to the world's largest mangrove forest, the Sundarbans.

flag_description: Vertical blue, gold and blue bands with a black broken trident in the center.
short_history: Barbados' history includes early Indigenous Amerindian settlement before English colonization began in 1627, establishing the island as one of Britain's most profitable Caribbean sugar colonies, built on a plantation economy dependent on enslaved African labor for over two centuries. Slavery was abolished across the British Empire in 1834. Barbados gained independence from Britain in 1966 while remaining a Commonwealth realm, and in 2021 the country transitioned to a republic, removing the British monarch as head of state and inaugurating its first president. Barbados is known for its stable democratic governance and reliance on tourism and international business.
interesting_fact: Barbados is one of the easternmost islands in the Caribbean.

flag_description: A red and green horizontal flag with a traditional ornamental pattern along the hoist.
short_history: Belarus's history includes its role as a core territory of medieval Kievan Rus and later incorporation into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth before Russian imperial annexation in the late eighteenth century. Belarus suffered enormous devastation and loss of life during World War II under Nazi occupation. It became a founding member of the Soviet Union and gained independence following the USSR's dissolution in 1991. Under President Alexander Lukashenko, in power since 1994, Belarus has maintained close political and economic ties with Russia while facing international criticism over its human rights record and authoritarian governance.
interesting_fact: Belarus contains extensive forests and is home to European bison.

flag_description: Three vertical black, yellow and red bands.
short_history: Belgium's history includes its historical position as part of the Low Countries and Burgundian and Habsburg territories before centuries of rule by Spanish, Austrian, French, and Dutch powers. Belgium gained independence from the Netherlands in 1830 following a popular revolution, establishing a constitutional monarchy. The country was invaded and occupied by Germany in both World War I and World War II despite its declared neutrality, and postwar Belgium became a founding member of the European Economic Community and later hosted the headquarters of the European Union and NATO in Brussels. Modern Belgium is a federal state balancing its Dutch-speaking Flemish and French-speaking Walloon communities.
interesting_fact: Brussels hosts major institutions of the European Union.

flag_description: A royal blue field with red stripes at the top and bottom and a central coat of arms.
short_history: Belize's history includes ancient Maya civilization, whose ruins remain scattered across the country, before British settlers arrived in the seventeenth century, initially for logwood and mahogany extraction. It became the colony of British Honduras and was long claimed by neighboring Guatemala, a territorial dispute that persists in modified form today. Belize gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1981, becoming the last British colony on the American mainland to do so. Since independence, Belize has developed a diverse, multiethnic society and an economy based on tourism, agriculture, and its extensive barrier reef, the second largest in the world.
interesting_fact: Belize is the only English-speaking country in mainland Central America.

flag_description: A green vertical band at the hoist and yellow and red horizontal bands.
short_history: Benin's history includes the powerful precolonial Kingdom of Dahomey, known for its elaborate court culture and, controversially, its deep involvement in the transatlantic slave trade, which made the coast a major departure point for enslaved Africans. France established colonial control in the late nineteenth century, and the territory became French Dahomey. Benin gained independence from France in 1960 and experienced significant political instability afterward, including multiple coups before a Marxist-Leninist government took power in 1972. The country transitioned peacefully to multiparty democracy in 1990, becoming an early model for democratic reform in Africa, and was renamed Benin in 1975.
interesting_fact: The historical Kingdom of Dahomey was located in present-day Benin.

independence_date: 8 August 1949 (Treaty of Friendship with India; never colonized)
flag_description: A yellow and orange diagonally divided flag featuring a white dragon.
short_history: Bhutan's history as an independent Himalayan kingdom developed under Buddhist influence, with the country unified in the seventeenth century by the Tibetan lama Ngawang Namgyal, who established a dual system of religious and civil governance. The Wangchuck dynasty founded Bhutan's hereditary monarchy in 1907, and the kingdom carefully managed relations with British India and later independent India while avoiding colonization. Bhutan pursued a deliberate policy of limited engagement with the outside world for much of the twentieth century, prioritizing cultural preservation. It transitioned to a constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament in 2008, and it is known internationally for measuring national progress through Gross National Happiness.
interesting_fact: Bhutan is famous for measuring national progress using Gross National Happiness.
aliases: Druk Yul, Land of the Thunder Dragon

capital: Sucre (constitutional capital); La Paz (seat of government)
languages: Spanish, Quechua, Aymara, and other Indigenous languages
short_history: Bolivia's history stretches from the ancient Tiwanaku civilization near Lake Titicaca through incorporation into the Inca Empire and nearly three centuries of Spanish colonial rule centered on the silver mines of Potosi. Independence was declared in 1825, and the new nation was named after liberator Simon Bolivar. The nineteenth and twentieth centuries brought territorial losses in regional wars, political instability, and the 1952 National Revolution, which introduced land reform and universal suffrage. Bolivia is unusual in having two capitals, with La Paz serving as the seat of government while Sucre remains the constitutional capital. Today the country is known for its Indigenous heritage and high-altitude landscapes.
interesting_fact: Bolivia has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

flag_description: The national flag of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
short_history: Bosnia and Herzegovina's history reflects centuries at the crossroads of empires, from early Slavic settlement through rule by the Ottoman Empire, which introduced Islam and shaped much of the region's cultural diversity, and later Austro-Hungarian administration after 1878. It became part of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia after World War I and remained part of socialist Yugoslavia until declaring independence in 1992. That declaration triggered a devastating war among Bosniaks, Serbs, and Croats that lasted until the 1995 Dayton Agreement established the country's current political structure of two entities. Sarajevo, the capital, hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics and later became a symbol of wartime resilience.
interesting_fact: Bosnia and Herzegovina has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Botswana's history includes long settlement by San and Bantu-speaking peoples before Tswana chiefdoms consolidated power across the region. In the late nineteenth century, local leaders sought British protection against expansion by neighboring powers, leading to the creation of the Bechuanaland Protectorate in 1885. Colonial administration remained relatively limited compared to many African territories. Botswana gained independence peacefully in 1966 under Seretse Khama, who became its first president. The subsequent discovery of diamonds transformed the economy, and Botswana is now frequently cited as one of Africa's most stable democracies and one of the continent's fastest-growing postcolonial economies.
interesting_fact: Botswana has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Brazil's history began with Indigenous peoples inhabiting the region for thousands of years before Portuguese explorer Pedro Alvares Cabral arrived in 1500, initiating over three centuries of colonial rule centered on sugar, gold, and later coffee production and reliant heavily on enslaved African labor. Brazil briefly served as the seat of the Portuguese empire when the royal court relocated there in 1808, and it achieved independence peacefully in 1822 under Emperor Pedro I, becoming a monarchy before transitioning to a republic in 1889. The twentieth century brought industrialization, periods of military rule from 1964 to 1985, and eventual democratization. Brazil is now South America's largest nation by population and economy.
interesting_fact: Brazil has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Uruguay, Argentina, Paraguay, Bolivia, Peru, Colombia, Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana

short_history: Brunei's history dates back to a powerful maritime sultanate that once controlled much of Borneo and parts of the Philippines between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries. Its influence declined over subsequent centuries due to internal conflict and European colonial expansion, and it became a British protectorate in 1888, retaining its sultanate under British oversight. Brunei achieved full independence in 1984, remaining one of the world's few absolute monarchies. The discovery of oil and natural gas in the early twentieth century transformed Brunei into one of the wealthiest nations in Southeast Asia, funding extensive social welfare programs for its citizens.
interesting_fact: Brunei has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Bulgaria's history traces back to the First Bulgarian Empire, founded in 681, one of the earliest medieval Slavic states in Europe, followed by a Second Bulgarian Empire before nearly five centuries of Ottoman rule beginning in the late fourteenth century. Bulgaria regained autonomy in 1878 following the Russo-Turkish War and full independence in 1908. The twentieth century brought involvement in the Balkan Wars and both World Wars, followed by decades as a communist state allied with the Soviet Union until 1989. Bulgaria transitioned to a multiparty democracy in the 1990s and joined the European Union in 2007, drawing on a rich heritage of Thracian, Slavic, and Ottoman influences.
interesting_fact: Bulgaria has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Romania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Greece, Türkiye

languages: French, and numerous Indigenous languages including Mossi
flag_description: The national flag of Burkina Faso.
short_history: Burkina Faso's history includes powerful precolonial kingdoms such as the Mossi states, which maintained centralized rule for centuries before French colonization in the late nineteenth century incorporated the territory into French West Africa as Upper Volta. The country achieved independence from France in 1960. Revolutionary leader Thomas Sankara renamed the nation Burkina Faso, meaning 'Land of Upright People,' in 1984 and pursued ambitious social and economic reforms before his assassination in 1987. Burkina Faso has since experienced periods of political instability, including several coups, most recently amid regional security challenges linked to armed insurgencies in the Sahel.
interesting_fact: Burkina Faso has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Mali, Niger, Benin, Togo, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire

short_history: Burundi's history features a centralized monarchy under a mwami, or king, that governed the region for centuries before German and later Belgian colonial rule grouped it with neighboring Rwanda as Ruanda-Urundi. Burundi gained independence in 1962 and initially retained its monarchy before becoming a republic in 1966. The following decades were marked by recurring ethnic violence between Hutu and Tutsi populations, including a brutal civil war from 1993 to 2005 that caused significant loss of life and displacement. A peace process led to power-sharing arrangements, and in 2019 the government relocated the political capital from Bujumbura to Gitega.
interesting_fact: Burundi has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Rwanda, Tanzania, Democratic Republic of the Congo

flag_description: The national flag of Cabo Verde.
short_history: Cabo Verde was uninhabited until Portuguese explorers settled the archipelago in the fifteenth century, making it one of the first European colonies in the tropics and an important hub in the transatlantic slave trade due to its strategic Atlantic location. Over centuries, a distinct Creole culture and language, Kriolu, emerged from the blending of Portuguese and West African influences. Cabo Verde gained independence from Portugal in 1975 following a liberation struggle led jointly with Guinea-Bissau. Since transitioning to multiparty democracy in 1991, it has become known for relative political stability, and its diaspora population abroad exceeds its resident population.
interesting_fact: Cabo Verde has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Cambodia's history includes the powerful Khmer Empire, which flourished from the ninth to fifteenth centuries and built the temple complex of Angkor Wat, among the largest religious monuments in the world. Following centuries of decline and pressure from neighboring kingdoms, Cambodia became a French protectorate in 1863 and gained independence in 1953. The country suffered immensely under the Khmer Rouge regime from 1975 to 1979, during which an estimated 1.5 to 2 million people died from executions, forced labor, and starvation. Cambodia has since rebuilt through a United Nations-backed peace process, transitioning to a constitutional monarchy with a developing economy.
interesting_fact: Cambodia has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Cameroon's history reflects its unusual colonial legacy, having been a German protectorate from 1884 before being divided between French and British administration after World War I under League of Nations mandates. This dual colonial heritage left lasting linguistic and administrative divisions between Francophone and Anglophone regions. French Cameroon gained independence in 1960, and the following year the British-administered southern region voted to join it, forming a united Cameroon. The country has since navigated tensions between its Anglophone and Francophone communities, including an ongoing separatist conflict in the Anglophone regions that began in 2016, alongside a diverse cultural and linguistic heritage often called 'Africa in miniature.'
interesting_fact: Cameroon has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Nigeria, Chad, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea

flag_description: A red-white-red vertical design with a red maple leaf in the center.
short_history: Canada's history began with Indigenous peoples who inhabited the land for thousands of years before French and British colonization from the sixteenth century onward established competing claims, culminating in British control after the 1763 Treaty of Paris. Canada became a self-governing federation in 1867 through the British North America Act, uniting several colonies, and it gradually gained full legislative independence, formalized by the Constitution Act of 1982, which patriated its constitution from Britain. The twentieth century saw Canada emerge as a major industrialized nation and a founding member of the United Nations and NATO. Today it is recognized for its bilingual French-English heritage, multiculturalism, and vast natural resources.
interesting_fact: Canada has the world's longest coastline.

flag_description: The national flag of Central African Republic.
short_history: The Central African Republic's history includes centuries of trade networks and small kingdoms before French colonization in the late nineteenth century incorporated the territory into French Equatorial Africa as Ubangi-Shari, a period marked by harsh forced-labor practices. The country gained independence from France in 1960. Its postcolonial history has been marked by chronic political instability, including a brief and infamous self-proclaimed empire under Jean-Bedel Bokassa in the 1970s and repeated coups. Since 2012, the country has experienced a prolonged conflict involving multiple armed factions, contributing to significant humanitarian crises despite the nation's substantial natural resource wealth, including diamonds and timber.
interesting_fact: Central African Republic has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Chad, Sudan, South Sudan, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Cameroon

short_history: Chad's history includes ancient trans-Saharan trade kingdoms such as Kanem-Bornu, which flourished for centuries around Lake Chad, before French colonization incorporated the territory into French Equatorial Africa in the late nineteenth century. Chad achieved independence from France in 1960, but the postcolonial period was soon marked by prolonged civil conflict between the largely Arab-Muslim north and the more Christian and animist south, compounded by foreign interventions from Libya and France. Political instability and periodic rebellions have continued into the twenty-first century. Despite the discovery of oil reserves in the early 2000s, Chad remains among the world's least developed nations.
interesting_fact: Chad has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Libya, Sudan, Central African Republic, Cameroon, Nigeria, Niger

short_history: Chile's history includes Indigenous peoples, notably the Mapuche, who resisted both Inca and later Spanish conquest for centuries. Spanish colonization began in the sixteenth century, and Chile declared independence in 1810, achieving it fully by 1818 under liberator Bernardo O'Higgins. The nineteenth and twentieth centuries brought territorial expansion, economic growth from nitrate and copper mining, and periods of democratic government interrupted by the 1973 military coup that installed General Augusto Pinochet's dictatorship, which lasted until 1990. Chile returned to democracy through a peaceful transition and has since become known for economic stability and one of the strongest economies in Latin America.
interesting_fact: Chile has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

flag_description: A red field with one large yellow star and four smaller yellow stars.
short_history: China's history spans thousands of years, encompassing successive dynasties from the Shang and Zhou through the Qin, which first unified the country in 221 BCE, to the Han, Tang, Song, Ming, and Qing dynasties, each contributing to a continuous civilization renowned for inventions, philosophy, and imperial governance. The Qing dynasty collapsed in 1912, giving way to a republic and decades of civil war and foreign invasion, including a devastating conflict with Japan. The People's Republic of China was established in 1949 following the Chinese Communist Party's victory in the civil war. Economic reforms beginning in 1978 transformed China into a global economic power while the Communist Party retained political control.
interesting_fact: China has one of the world's oldest continuous civilizations.
neighbors: Mongolia, Russia, North Korea, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Laos, Vietnam

flag_description: Horizontal yellow, blue and red bands, with the yellow band twice the height of the other two.
short_history: Colombia's history includes Indigenous civilizations such as the Muisca before Spanish conquest in the sixteenth century established it as part of the Viceroyalty of New Granada. Colombia declared independence from Spain in 1810, with independence secured by 1819 under Simon Bolivar, initially as part of Gran Colombia before separating into its own republic in 1831. The nineteenth and twentieth centuries were marked by recurring civil conflicts, including a decades-long internal armed conflict involving guerrilla groups, paramilitaries, and drug cartels that began in the 1960s. A landmark 2016 peace agreement with the FARC guerrilla group marked a major step toward ending one of the world's longest-running conflicts.
interesting_fact: Colombia is one of the world's most biodiverse countries.

short_history: Comoros' history reflects its position along historic Indian Ocean trade routes, which brought Arab, Persian, African, and Malagasy influences to the islands well before European contact. France established colonial control over the archipelago in the nineteenth century. Comoros gained independence in 1975, though the island of Mayotte voted to remain under French administration, a dispute that continues today. Since independence, Comoros has experienced remarkable political instability, including more than twenty attempted or successful coups, making it one of the most coup-prone nations in the world, alongside ongoing efforts toward political and economic stabilization.
interesting_fact: Comoros has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: The Republic of the Congo's history includes the precolonial Kongo Kingdom before French colonization established the territory as part of French Equatorial Africa in the late nineteenth century, with Brazzaville serving as the colonial federation's capital. The country gained independence from France in 1960. It adopted a Marxist-Leninist government for a period during the Cold War before transitioning toward multiparty politics in the early 1990s. Civil conflicts in the mid-to-late 1990s caused significant disruption, and the country has since relied heavily on oil exports, which dominate its economy, while working to diversify and address ongoing governance challenges.
interesting_fact: Congo has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.
neighbors: Gabon, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Angola (Cabinda exclave)

flag_description: Blue, white and red horizontal bands with the red band in the center.
short_history: Costa Rica's history includes Indigenous societies that predated Spanish colonization beginning in the sixteenth century, though the territory attracted relatively limited Spanish settlement due to its lack of easily exploitable mineral wealth. Costa Rica gained independence from Spain in 1821 as part of the broader Central American independence movement, briefly joining the Federal Republic of Central America before becoming fully sovereign in 1838. In 1948, following a brief civil war, Costa Rica famously abolished its military, redirecting resources toward education and healthcare. This decision, combined with sustained democratic governance, has made Costa Rica one of Latin America's most stable and prosperous nations.
interesting_fact: Costa Rica abolished its military in 1948.

flag_description: Red, white and blue horizontal bands with the Croatian coat of arms.
short_history: Croatia's history dates to the early medieval Croatian kingdom established around the tenth century, followed by a long union with Hungary and later incorporation into the Habsburg monarchy. Croatia became part of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes after World War I, later renamed Yugoslavia, and remained part of socialist Yugoslavia after World War II. Croatia declared independence in 1991, an act that triggered a war lasting until 1995 as Croatian forces sought to establish control over the entire country. Since the war's end, Croatia has rebuilt its economy around tourism along the Adriatic coast and joined the European Union in 2013.
interesting_fact: Croatia has a long Adriatic coastline with numerous islands.
neighbors: Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro

flag_description: Five alternating blue and white stripes with a red triangle and white star.
short_history: Cuba's history includes Indigenous Taino inhabitants largely displaced following Spanish colonization beginning in 1492, after which the island became a major center of sugar production reliant on enslaved African labor. Cuba achieved independence from Spain in 1898 following the Spanish-American War, though it remained under significant United States influence for decades afterward. Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution overthrew the Batista dictatorship and established a socialist one-party state aligned with the Soviet Union during the Cold War, prompting a lasting United States trade embargo. Cuba has continued under Communist Party rule into the twenty-first century while gradually introducing limited economic reforms.
interesting_fact: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

short_history: Cyprus's history stretches back to ancient Greek and Phoenician settlement, followed by successive rule under Roman, Byzantine, Lusignan, Venetian, and Ottoman powers before becoming a British colony in 1878, formalized in 1914. Cyprus gained independence from Britain in 1960. Intercommunal tensions between the Greek Cypriot majority and Turkish Cypriot minority culminated in a 1974 coup and subsequent Turkish military intervention, dividing the island into a Greek Cypriot south and a Turkish Cypriot north, the latter recognized only by Türkiye. The Republic of Cyprus joined the European Union in 2004, while reunification talks between the two communities have continued intermittently without resolution.
interesting_fact: Cyprus has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

flag_description: The national flag of Czech Republic.
short_history: The Czech Republic's history traces back to the medieval Kingdom of Bohemia, a influential and prosperous state within the Holy Roman Empire, followed by centuries of Habsburg rule after 1526. Czechoslovakia was established in 1918 following the collapse of Austria-Hungary, uniting Czechs and Slovaks, though it was later annexed by Nazi Germany in 1938 and 1939. After World War II, Czechoslovakia fell under communist rule until the peaceful Velvet Revolution of 1989 restored democracy. The country then split amicably from Slovakia in the 1993 Velvet Divorce, forming the independent Czech Republic, which later joined NATO and the European Union.

flag_description: The national flag of Cote d'Ivoire.

Following his death in 1993, the country experienced growing political and ethnic tensions that erupted into civil wars in 2002 and again after the disputed 2010 election. Belgium took direct control in 1908, and the country gained independence in 1960 amid immediate political turmoil, including the assassination of independence leader Patrice Lumumba. Decades of dictatorship under Mobutu Sese Seko followed, and since the 1990s the country has endured repeated conflicts, including wars drawing in multiple neighboring states, despite immense mineral wealth.

neighbors: Republic of the Congo, Central African Republic, South Sudan, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, Zambia, Angola

short_history: Denmark's history includes the Viking Age, from roughly the eighth to eleventh centuries, when Danish seafarers raided, traded, and settled across Europe. Denmark's monarchy, tracing back over a thousand years, is among the oldest continuously reigning royal houses in the world. The kingdom once controlled Norway, parts of Sweden, and territories abroad, but it steadily lost power and territory through wars, including the loss of Norway in 1814 and Schleswig to Prussia in 1864. Denmark was occupied by Nazi Germany during World War II despite declaring neutrality. Postwar Denmark developed an extensive welfare state and joined the European Union in 1973.
interesting_fact: The Danish flag is commonly considered one of the world's oldest continuously used national flags.

short_history: Djibouti's history reflects its strategic position at the entrance to the Red Sea, long used by Afar and Somali peoples and by Arab traders navigating routes between Africa, the Middle East, and Asia. France established colonial control in the late nineteenth century, naming the territory French Somaliland and later the French Territory of the Afars and Issas. Djibouti gained independence from France in 1977. Its strategic location has since made it host to multiple foreign military bases, including French, American, and Chinese installations, and Djibouti's economy relies heavily on its port and shipping activity serving landlocked Ethiopia.
interesting_fact: Djibouti has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Dominica's history includes the Kalinago people, the last significant Indigenous Caribbean population still residing on ancestral land in the region, who resisted European colonization longer than on most other Caribbean islands due to the island's rugged, mountainous terrain. Contested between France and Britain for control, Dominica ultimately became a British colony in 1763. It gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1978, becoming a republic rather than retaining the British monarch as head of state. Known as the 'Nature Island' for its rainforests and volcanic landscape, Dominica has focused its economy on ecotourism and agriculture, notably bananas.
interesting_fact: Dominica has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

flag_description: The national flag of Dominican Republic.
short_history: The Dominican Republic's history includes the Indigenous Taino population before Spanish colonization established Santo Domingo in 1496 as the first permanent European settlement in the Americas. The country shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti and experienced a complicated history of Haitian occupation from 1822 to 1844, after which it declared independence. The nineteenth and twentieth centuries brought recurring instability, a period of United States occupation, and the long dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo from 1930 to 1961, one of Latin America's most repressive regimes. Since transitioning to democracy, the Dominican Republic has developed a tourism-driven economy.
interesting_fact: Dominican Republic has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Ecuador's history includes Indigenous civilizations later absorbed into the Inca Empire before Spanish conquest in the sixteenth century established Quito as a major colonial administrative center. Ecuador gained independence from Spain in the 1820s, initially as part of Gran Colombia before becoming a separate republic in 1830. The nineteenth and twentieth centuries brought recurring political instability and border disputes with Peru, resolved through a 1998 peace treaty. Ecuador is notable for the Galapagos Islands, which inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution, and for adopting the US dollar as its official currency in 2000 following an economic crisis.
interesting_fact: Ecuador has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

flag_description: Red, white and black horizontal bands with the golden Eagle of Saladin.
short_history: Egypt's history spans over five thousand years, encompassing the ancient pharaonic civilization that built the pyramids and developed hieroglyphic writing, followed by Persian, Greek, and Roman rule, and the Arab conquest in the seventh century, which brought Islam and the Arabic language. Egypt later came under Ottoman and then British influence, becoming a British protectorate in 1914. It gained nominal independence in 1922, though British influence persisted until the 1952 revolution led by Gamal Abdel Nasser overthrew the monarchy and established a republic in 1953. Egypt has since played a central role in Arab politics, including a landmark 1979 peace treaty with Israel and the 2011 Arab Spring uprising.
interesting_fact: The ancient pyramids of Giza are among the world's most famous monuments.

flag_description: The national flag of El Salvador.
short_history: El Salvador's history includes Indigenous Pipil and Lenca populations before Spanish colonization in the sixteenth century. It gained independence from Spain in 1821, briefly joining the Federal Republic of Central America before becoming fully sovereign in 1841. The twentieth century was marked by significant social inequality that contributed to a brutal civil war from 1980 to 1992 between the government and leftist guerrillas, resulting in an estimated 75,000 deaths and prompting substantial emigration, particularly to the United States. Since a peace agreement ended the conflict, El Salvador has worked to rebuild institutions while facing challenges from gang violence and, more recently, an intensive government crackdown on organized crime.
interesting_fact: El Salvador has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

flag_description: The national flag of Equatorial Guinea.
short_history: Equatorial Guinea's history includes Bantu migration and Portuguese exploration before Spain acquired the territory in 1778, making it the only Spanish-speaking country in Sub-Saharan Africa. It gained independence from Spain in 1968, but the new nation quickly fell under the brutal dictatorship of Francisco Macias Nguema, whose rule caused mass killings and emigration until he was overthrown in a 1979 coup led by his nephew, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, who remains president. The discovery of substantial offshore oil reserves in the 1990s transformed the country's wealth on paper, though this wealth has not been broadly distributed among the population.
interesting_fact: Equatorial Guinea has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Eritrea's history includes ancient trade links along the Red Sea coast and periods of Ottoman and Egyptian influence before Italy established a colony there in 1890. After World War II, Eritrea was federated with, and later annexed by, Ethiopia, a move that sparked a thirty-year armed independence struggle beginning in 1961. Eritrea achieved independence in 1993 following a referendum after Ethiopian forces were defeated. A subsequent border war with Ethiopia from 1998 to 2000 caused heavy casualties, and Eritrea has since been governed under a single-party system with indefinite national service requirements, contributing to significant emigration.
interesting_fact: Eritrea has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Estonia's history includes centuries of rule by Danish, German, Swedish, and Russian powers before it briefly achieved independence in 1918 following World War I and the Russian Revolution. Estonia was forcibly annexed by the Soviet Union in 1940 under the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, then occupied by Nazi Germany, before Soviet control resumed after World War II, accompanied by mass deportations. Estonia regained independence in 1991 during the Soviet Union's collapse, notably through the peaceful 'Singing Revolution' of mass demonstrations. Since independence, Estonia has developed a highly digitized economy and government, and it joined both NATO and the European Union in 2004.
interesting_fact: Estonia has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Eswatini's history as a Swazi kingdom developed in the early nineteenth century under King Sobhuza I, who consolidated various clans into a unified nation. The kingdom became a British protectorate in the late nineteenth century amid competing colonial claims from Britain and the Boers. Eswatini, then known as Swaziland, gained independence from Britain in 1968 as a constitutional monarchy, though King Sobhuza II suspended the constitution in 1973 and assumed absolute power. The country remains one of the world's last absolute monarchies, ruled since 1986 by King Mswati III, and was officially renamed Eswatini in 2018.

The ancient monarchy ended in 1974 when Emperor Haile Selassie was overthrown by a Marxist military junta, which ruled until 1991 amid famine and civil war. Ethiopia has since experienced periods of rapid economic growth alongside continued ethnic and political conflict, including a devastating civil war in the Tigray region from 2020 to 2022.
interesting_fact: Ethiopia uses a calendar system with 13 months.
neighbors: Eritrea, Djibouti, Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan, Sudan

short_history: Fiji's history includes Melanesian and Polynesian settlement dating back over three thousand years, developing a complex chiefly society before European contact. Britain established colonial rule in 1874, and colonial administrators subsequently brought large numbers of Indian indentured laborers to work on sugar plantations, creating lasting demographic and political divisions between Indigenous Fijians and Indo-Fijians. Fiji gained independence from Britain in 1970. The following decades saw repeated political instability and several military coups, often linked to ethnic tensions between the two communities, most recently in 2006. Fiji has since worked toward democratic consolidation while remaining a major tourism destination in the South Pacific.
interesting_fact: Fiji has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Finland's history includes several centuries as part of the Swedish kingdom before being ceded to Russia in 1809 as an autonomous Grand Duchy. Finland declared independence in 1917, taking advantage of the Russian Revolution's upheaval. It fought two wars against the Soviet Union during World War II, the Winter War and Continuation War, successfully preserving its independence despite territorial losses. Postwar Finland pursued a careful policy of neutrality during the Cold War while developing a strong welfare state and technology sector. Finland joined the European Union in 1995 and, prompted by Russia's invasion of Ukraine, joined NATO in 2023, ending decades of military non-alignment.
interesting_fact: Finland has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

The nineteenth and twentieth centuries brought Napoleon's empire, colonial expansion, two devastating World Wars fought partly on French soil, and German occupation from 1940 to 1944. Postwar France became a founding member of the European Union and remains a major global economic, cultural, and military power.

short_history: Gabon's history includes Bantu-speaking peoples who settled the region over centuries before French colonization in the nineteenth century, with the capital Libreville founded in 1849 as a settlement for freed slaves. Gabon became part of French Equatorial Africa and gained independence from France in 1960. The country was governed for over four decades by President Omar Bongo, who maintained close ties with France, and later by his son Ali Bongo, whose 2023 removal in a military coup ended over fifty years of Bongo family rule. Gabon's economy has long relied on oil exports alongside significant timber and mineral resources.
interesting_fact: Gabon has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: The Gambia's history is shaped by its position along the Gambia River, which made it a corridor for trade, including the transatlantic slave trade, and later a narrow British colonial territory surrounded almost entirely by French Senegal. The Gambia gained independence from Britain in 1965 and briefly formed a confederation with Senegal called Senegambia in the 1980s before it dissolved. The country was ruled for over two decades by President Yahya Jammeh, who seized power in a 1994 coup, until his defeat in the 2016 election and eventual departure following regional diplomatic and military pressure, marking a democratic transition.
interesting_fact: Gambia has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Georgia's history includes ancient kingdoms and an early adoption of Christianity in the fourth century, followed by centuries of invasions by Persian, Arab, Mongol, and Ottoman forces before Russian imperial annexation in the early nineteenth century. Georgia briefly achieved independence in 1918 before Soviet annexation in 1921. It restored independence in 1991 amid the Soviet Union's collapse, though the following decades brought internal conflicts in the breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia, culminating in a brief war with Russia in 2008. Georgia has since pursued closer ties with Europe and NATO while continuing to navigate tensions with Russia.
interesting_fact: Georgia has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Germany's history includes centuries as a fragmented collection of kingdoms and principalities within the Holy Roman Empire before Prussia led the unification of a modern German nation-state in 1871. After 1945, Germany was divided into capitalist West Germany and communist East Germany during the Cold War, symbolized by the Berlin Wall built in 1961. Germany peacefully reunified in 1990 following the wall's fall, and it has since become the largest economy in Europe and a leading member of the European Union.
interesting_fact: Germany has one of Europe's largest economies.
neighbors: Denmark, Poland, Czech Republic, Austria, Switzerland, France, Luxembourg, Belgium, Netherlands

short_history: Ghana's history includes the powerful precolonial Ashanti Empire, known for its gold wealth and sophisticated political organization, before British colonization established the Gold Coast colony in the nineteenth century. Ghana made history in 1957 by becoming the first Sub-Saharan African colony to achieve independence, under the leadership of Kwame Nkrumah, a milestone that inspired independence movements across the continent. Nkrumah was overthrown in a 1966 coup, beginning decades of political instability and military rule. Ghana returned to stable multiparty democracy in 1992 and has since become widely regarded as one of Africa's more stable democracies and steadily growing economies.
interesting_fact: Ghana has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Greece's history includes ancient civilizations that laid foundations for Western philosophy, democracy, theater, and science, followed by the classical era of city-states such as Athens and Sparta and later incorporation into the Roman and Byzantine Empires. Greece fell under nearly four centuries of Ottoman rule before winning independence through a war fought from 1821 to 1829, aided by European powers. The twentieth century brought territorial expansion, occupation during World War II, a subsequent civil war, and a military dictatorship from 1967 to 1974 before democracy was restored. Greece joined the European Union in 1981 and has remained influential through its classical heritage and Mediterranean tourism industry.

short_history: Grenada's history includes Indigenous Carib inhabitants before French colonization in the seventeenth century, followed by British control from 1763, during which the island developed a plantation economy based on nutmeg and other spices, earning it the nickname 'Spice Isle.' Grenada gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1974. short_history: Guatemala's history includes the ancient Maya civilization, which built major cities such as Tikal in the region long before Spanish conquest in the 1520s established colonial rule centered in Guatemala City. The twentieth century included a 1954 US-backed coup that ousted a democratically elected government, followed by a devastating 36-year civil war from 1960 to 1996 that disproportionately affected Indigenous Maya communities and was later recognized as including acts of genocide. interesting_fact: Guatemala has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Guinea's history includes the medieval Mali and Songhai empires and later smaller Fulani and Mandinka states before French colonization in the late nineteenth century incorporated the territory into French West Africa. Under founding president Sekou Toure, Guinea pursued a socialist path marked by repression until his death in 1984. The country has since experienced further periods of authoritarian rule and military coups, including one in 2021, alongside substantial bauxite and mineral wealth.

Guinea-Bissau declared independence in 1973, formally recognized by Portugal in 1974 following the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon. short_history: Guyana's history includes Indigenous Arawak and Carib peoples before Dutch, and later British, colonization established plantations reliant first on enslaved African labor and later on indentured laborers from India following abolition, shaping the country's ethnically diverse population. British Guiana gained independence from the United Kingdom in 1966 and became a republic in 1970. Political life since independence has often reflected ethnic divisions between Afro-Guyanese and Indo-Guyanese communities. A long-standing border dispute with Venezuela over the oil-rich Essequibo region has intensified in recent years following major offshore oil discoveries that have rapidly transformed Guyana's economy.
interesting_fact: Guyana has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Haiti's history includes French colonization that made Saint-Domingue one of the most profitable plantation colonies in the world, built on the brutal exploitation of enslaved Africans. In 1804, following a thirteen-year revolution led by figures including Toussaint Louverture, Haiti became the first Black republic and the first nation to abolish slavery through revolution, though it was forced to pay a crippling indemnity to France for decades afterward. The twentieth century brought United States occupation, the repressive Duvalier family dictatorship from 1957 to 1986, and continued political instability. short_history: Honduras's history includes the Maya civilization, notably the ruins at Copan, before Spanish conquest in the sixteenth century. Honduras gained independence from Spain in 1821, briefly joining the Federal Republic of Central America before becoming fully sovereign. In the twentieth century, extensive banana cultivation by American companies gave rise to the term 'banana republic,' reflecting the outsized influence of foreign corporations over politics and economy. Honduras has experienced periods of military rule and, more recently, significant instability following a 2009 coup, alongside high rates of gang violence that have driven substantial emigration, particularly to the United States.

Hungary lost roughly two-thirds of its territory under the 1920 Treaty of Trianon following World War I. After World War II, Hungary became a communist state, experiencing a suppressed uprising in 1956, before transitioning to democracy in 1989. short_history: Iceland's history began with Norse and Celtic settlement in the ninth century, and in 930 CE settlers established the Althing, often considered one of the world's oldest surviving parliaments. The postwar period brought disputes with Britain over fishing rights, known as the Cod Wars, and later a severe banking collapse in 2008 that devastated the economy. Iceland has since recovered strongly, developing a robust economy centered on tourism, fishing, and renewable geothermal energy.

British colonial rule, established through the East India Company and later direct crown control, lasted nearly two centuries before India gained independence in 1947 following a nonviolent movement led by Mahatma Gandhi. Independence was accompanied by the traumatic partition of British India into India and Pakistan, displacing millions. India became a republic in 1950 and has since grown into the world's most populous nation and a major global economic and technological power.

Japan occupied the islands during World War II, and Indonesian nationalists proclaimed independence in 1945 immediately after Japan's surrender, though the Netherlands did not formally recognize independence until 1949 following armed conflict. Indonesia developed under founding president Sukarno and later the authoritarian New Order regime of Suharto, which ruled from 1967 to 1998. Since Suharto's fall, Indonesia has become the world's largest Muslim-majority nation and a growing democracy with the largest economy in Southeast Asia.

The Safavid dynasty established Shia Islam as the state religion in the sixteenth century. In the twentieth century, the Pahlavi dynasty pursued modernization until the 1979 Islamic Revolution, led by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, overthrew the monarchy and established an Islamic republic. Iran subsequently fought a devastating eight-year war with Iraq in the 1980s and has remained a major, often contested, regional power.

A 1958 coup ended the monarchy, and the Baath Party, eventually led by Saddam Hussein from 1979, established an authoritarian government responsible for a costly war with Iran in the 1980s and the 1990 invasion of Kuwait. short_history: Ireland's history includes ancient Celtic culture and a rich monastic tradition during the early medieval period, followed by Norman invasion in the twelfth century and centuries of increasing English and later British control. Following the 1916 Easter Rising and a subsequent war of independence, most of Ireland gained independence in 1922, with the remaining six northern counties staying part of the United Kingdom. Italy was unified into a single kingdom in 1861 through the Risorgimento movement led by figures such as Giuseppe Garibaldi. The twentieth century brought Benito Mussolini's fascist dictatorship, alliance with Nazi Germany in World War II, and postwar transition to a republic in 1946. Italy became a founding member of the European Union and remains one of the world's major economies.

short_history: Jamaica's history includes the Indigenous Taino people before Spanish colonization in 1494, followed by British conquest in 1655, after which the island became one of the world's largest sugar producers, built on the forced labor of enslaved Africans. Jamaica also became a center of Maroon resistance, as escaped enslaved people established independent communities in the mountainous interior. Slavery was abolished in 1834, and Jamaica gained independence from Britain in 1962. The country has since become internationally influential through its music, particularly reggae, and cultural figures such as Bob Marley, while continuing to develop its tourism-based economy.

The 1868 Meiji Restoration ended feudal rule and launched rapid modernization and industrialization, transforming Japan into a major imperial power that expanded across East Asia. Japan's defeat in World War II, including the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, led to postwar demilitarization and a new constitution. Japan subsequently achieved remarkable economic recovery, becoming one of the world's largest and most technologically advanced economies.

Jordan has since played a central role in regional diplomacy despite limited natural resources, absorbing large numbers of refugees from multiple regional conflicts, including Palestinians after 1948 and 1967, and more recently Syrians and Iraqis, while maintaining relative stability under continuous Hashemite rule.

short_history: Kazakhstan's history includes centuries of nomadic Turkic and Mongol tribes traversing the vast steppe along Silk Road trade routes before Russian imperial expansion incorporated the region in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Kazakhstan gained independence with the Soviet Union's dissolution in 1991. Since independence, under long-serving president Nursultan Nazarbayev and his successor, Kazakhstan has leveraged vast oil, gas, and mineral wealth to become Central Asia's largest economy, while pursuing a multi-vector foreign policy balancing Russia, China, and the West.
interesting_fact: Kazakhstan has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Kenya's history includes early human origins, with some of the world's oldest hominid fossils discovered in the region, and centuries of Swahili coastal trade with the Arab world before British colonization established Kenya as a settler colony in the early twentieth century. The Mau Mau uprising in the 1950s, a violent anticolonial rebellion met with harsh British suppression, hastened the push toward independence, achieved in 1963 under Jomo Kenyatta. Kenya has since developed into East Africa's largest economy and a regional hub for finance and technology, while navigating periodic ethnic and political tensions, including violence following the disputed 2007 election.
interesting_fact: Kenya has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Kiribati's history includes Micronesian settlement of its scattered atolls thousands of years ago, followed by British colonization in the late nineteenth century as part of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony. The Gilbert Islands were the site of intense fighting between American and Japanese forces during World War II, notably the Battle of Tarawa in 1943. The islands gained independence from Britain in 1979, becoming the Republic of Kiribati after the Ellice Islands separated to form Tuvalu. interesting_fact: Kiribati has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

Kuwait became a British protectorate in 1899 to guard against Ottoman expansion and gained full independence in 1961. The discovery of oil in the 1930s transformed Kuwait into one of the wealthiest nations in the world per capita. Kuwait was invaded and occupied by Iraq in 1990, prompting the international Gulf War coalition that liberated the country in 1991. Portugal's power declined over subsequent centuries, and it endured a long authoritarian dictatorship under Antonio Salazar from the 1930s until the 1974 Carnation Revolution restored democracy. short_history: Qatar's history includes centuries of pearl diving and fishing along the Persian Gulf coast before the Al Thani family established control in the mid-nineteenth century, a dynasty that continues to rule today. The twentieth century brought territorial gains after World War I, alliance with Nazi Germany followed by a late switch to the Allies in World War II, and decades of harsh communist rule under Nicolae Ceausescu, whose regime was violently overthrown in the 1989 revolution, one of the few Eastern Bloc transitions marked by significant bloodshed. Romania joined NATO in 2004 and the European Union in 2007.

Saint Kitts and Nevis achieved independence from Britain in 1983, becoming the smallest sovereign state in the Americas by both area and population. Saint Lucia gained independence from Britain in 1979. Since independence, the island has developed a tourism-driven economy centered on its dramatic volcanic Piton peaks, while retaining the British monarch as head of state within the Commonwealth.

short_history: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' history includes the Garifuna people, descended from Indigenous Kalinago and shipwrecked or escaped African slaves, who fiercely resisted European colonization for over a century before Britain gained control in 1783 and later deported many Garifuna to Central America. The islands developed a plantation economy before Britain abolished slavery in 1834. Saint Vincent and the Grenadines gained independence from Britain in 1979. The multi-island nation has since built an economy based on agriculture, notably bananas, and a growing tourism sector centered on its scenic Grenadine islands, while remaining a Commonwealth realm under the British monarch.
interesting_fact: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

short_history: Samoa's history includes Polynesian settlement dating back roughly three thousand years, developing one of the oldest and most influential Polynesian cultures, from which other Pacific societies trace ancestral ties. Germany and the United States divided the Samoan islands in 1899 following a period of competing colonial interest, with Germany administering what is now independent Samoa and the United States retaining American Samoa. flag_description: The national flag of San Marino.
short_history: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving sovereign state and republic, tracing its founding to 301 CE when, according to tradition, a Christian stonemason named Marinus established a small community on Mount Titano to escape religious persecution. The republic maintained its independence through the Middle Ages and the Italian unification of the nineteenth century, in part due to diplomatic goodwill earned by sheltering refugees, including supporters of Giuseppe Garibaldi. San Marino remained neutral during both World Wars. The microstate, entirely surrounded by Italy, has since built a prosperous economy based on tourism, banking, and light manufacturing, retaining its historic system of two co-heads of state elected every six months.
interesting_fact: San Marino has unique cultural, geographic and historical characteristics.

official_name: Democratic Republic of Sao Tome and Principe

Sao Tome and Principe gained independence from Portugal in 1975. The small island nation adopted a single-party socialist system before transitioning to multiparty democracy in the early 1990s. short_history: Saudi Arabia's history includes its role as the birthplace of Islam in the seventh century CE, with the holy cities of Mecca and Medina making it central to the Muslim world ever since. The modern state was founded in 1932 by King Abdulaziz Ibn Saud, who unified various regions of the Arabian Peninsula through a combination of military campaigns and alliances, including with the religiously influential Wahhabi movement. The discovery of massive oil reserves in the 1930s transformed Saudi Arabia into one of the world's most influential energy powers and wealthiest nations. In recent years, the kingdom has pursued significant social and economic reforms under Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, including efforts to diversify its oil-dependent economy through the Vision 2030 initiative.
interesting_fact: Saudi Arabia contains the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

short_history: Senegal's history includes the medieval Jolof Empire and later coastal trading posts established by European powers, with the island of Goree becoming a notorious hub of the transatlantic slave trade under Portuguese, Dutch, and French control. France established Senegal as the administrative center of French West Africa, and Dakar became one of colonial Africa's most developed cities. Senegal gained independence from France in 1960 under Leopold Sedar Senghor, a renowned poet and Africa's first democratically elected president to voluntarily leave office. Senegal has since maintained a reputation as one of Africa's more stable democracies, notably never having experienced a successful military coup.

short_history: Serbia's history includes a powerful medieval kingdom and empire before falling under Ottoman rule following the pivotal 1389 Battle of Kosovo, an event that remains central to Serbian national identity. Serbia played a central role in the outbreak of World War I following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo by a Bosnian Serb nationalist. Seychelles gained independence from Britain in 1976. Britain formally established a colony and protectorate over the wider territory in 1808 and 1896 respectively. Sierra Leone gained independence in 1961. The country endured a brutal eleven-year civil war from 1991 to 2002, notorious for its use of child soldiers and the trade in conflict, or 'blood,' diamonds that helped finance the fighting. Since the war's end, Sierra Leone has focused on postwar recovery and rebuilding its diamond and agricultural sectors.

short_history: Singapore's history as a major trading post began in 1819 when Sir Stamford Raffles established a British trading settlement, capitalizing on its strategic location along key maritime shipping routes. Singapore fell under a brutal Japanese occupation during World War II before returning to British administration. It joined the Federation of Malaysia in 1963 but separated just two years later, in 1965, becoming an independent city-state under founding leader Lee Kuan Yew. Despite lacking natural resources, Singapore transformed within a few decades into one of the world's wealthiest nations and leading global financial and trade hubs through disciplined economic planning.

short_history: Slovakia's history includes the medieval Great Moravian Empire and centuries as part of the Kingdom of Hungary before Slovaks united with Czechs to form Czechoslovakia in 1918 following the collapse of Austria-Hungary. Slovakia peacefully separated from the Czech Republic in the 1993 Velvet Divorce, forming its own independent state. short_history: Slovenia's history includes centuries under Habsburg Austrian rule before it joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes after World War I, later part of socialist Yugoslavia. Slovenia was the first Yugoslav republic to declare independence, in 1991, and experienced only a brief ten-day war before achieving separation, avoiding the prolonged violence that engulfed other parts of former Yugoslavia. Slovenia subsequently pursued rapid integration with Western Europe, joining both NATO and the European Union in 2004 and adopting the euro in 2007, making it one of the most economically successful of the former Yugoslav states.

The Solomon Islands gained independence from Britain in 1978. The country experienced significant ethnic tension and violence between 1998 and 2003, prompting a regional peacekeeping intervention, and it has more recently navigated shifting geopolitical alignments, including a controversial 2022 security agreement with China.

short_history: Somalia's history includes ancient trade links along the Horn of Africa coast and various Islamic sultanates before the territory was divided into British and Italian colonial zones in the late nineteenth century. South Korea endured postwar poverty and periods of authoritarian military rule before achieving what is often called the 'Miracle on the Han River,' a rapid economic transformation into a major industrial and technology power beginning in the 1960s. short_history: Togo's history includes various ethnic kingdoms before Germany established a protectorate in 1884, which was later divided between France and Britain as League of Nations mandates following Germany's defeat in World War I. short_history: Tonga's history includes a Polynesian maritime empire that, centuries ago, exerted influence across a wide swath of the Pacific under the Tu'i Tonga dynasty. The two islands, historically administered separately, were unified as a single British colony in 1889. Trinidad and Tobago gained independence from Britain in 1962 and became a republic in 1976. Substantial oil and natural gas reserves have made it one of the wealthier nations in the Caribbean, while the islands are also renowned as the birthplace of steelpan music and vibrant Carnival celebrations.

short_history: Tunisia's history includes ancient Carthage, a powerful Phoenician city-state that rivaled Rome before its destruction in 146 BCE, followed by Roman, Vandal, Byzantine, and Arab rule beginning in the seventh century, which brought Islam and Arabic language and culture. short_history: Turkmenistan's history includes ancient Silk Road cities such as Merv, once among the largest cities in the world, and centuries of Turkic nomadic culture before Russian imperial conquest in the late nineteenth century and subsequent incorporation into the Soviet Union. The country has since been governed under a highly centralized and secretive authoritarian system, first under President Saparmurat Niyazov, who cultivated an extensive personality cult until his death in 2006, and subsequently under Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov and his son. short_history: Tuvalu's history includes Polynesian settlement of its nine small atolls over many centuries, followed by British colonial administration as part of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands. With a highest point of only about five meters above sea level, Tuvalu has become one of the most prominent international voices warning about the existential threat of climate change and rising sea levels, and it has explored measures including a digital 'nation' backup and relocation agreements to preserve its sovereignty and culture.

Following the Ottoman Empire's collapse after World War I, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk led a war of independence and founded the modern secular Republic of Türkiye in 1923, implementing sweeping reforms to modernize and Westernize the new state. Türkiye has since navigated periods of military intervention in politics, a failed 2016 coup attempt, and a shift under President Recep Tayyip Erdogan toward a more centralized presidential system and a more prominent, sometimes assertive, role in regional affairs, all while straddling a unique position bridging Europe and Asia.

Uganda experienced further conflict, including a long insurgency by the Lord's Resistance Army in the north, before achieving greater stability under President Yoweri Museveni, in power since 1986, one of Africa's longest-serving leaders.

short_history: Ukraine's history includes the medieval state of Kievan Rus, considered a shared ancestor of Russian, Ukrainian, and Belarusian identity, followed by centuries of rule by Polish-Lithuanian, and later Russian imperial, powers. Ukraine briefly gained independence after World War I before being absorbed into the Soviet Union, where it endured the Holodomor, a devastating man-made famine in 1932 and 1933 that killed millions. Ukraine achieved independence with the Soviet Union's dissolution in 1991. The country's post-Soviet history has been shaped by tension between pro-Western and pro-Russian political currents, including the 2014 Euromaidan revolution and Russia's subsequent annexation of Crimea, escalating into a full-scale Russian invasion in February 2022 that continues to define Ukraine's present.
interesting_fact: Ukraine is one of Europe's largest countries by area.
neighbors: Belarus, Russia, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Moldova
